rationale.conceptual: The DFT workflow uses well-documented methods (plane-wave GGA, finite-displacement phonons, strain-stress elastic constants) that are non-trivial but not novel; the main difficulty lies in correctly implementing the supercell construction, convergence, and post-processing of multiple properties – an established multi-part algorithm.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves about 6 sequential stages with dependencies (structure generation, relaxation, formation energy, phonon calculation, elastic constants, aggregation). While tools (Quantum ESPRESSO, Phonopy) are standard, orchestrating the full flow and ensuring convergence across stages constitutes a multi-stage pipeline of moderate complexity.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires standard DFT calculations to reproduce elastic and stability properties of a TiN/WN₀.₅ superlattice. The methods (supercell relaxation, formation energy, phonon DOS, elastic constants via strain-stress) are established but involve multiple interacting components and careful convergence; the workflow is multi-stage (structure generation, relaxation, formation energy, phonon, elastic constants, reporting) but uses common tools. Resource needs are moderate: a 128-atom supercell DFT run on CPUs, no GPU required.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT calculations for a ~128‑atom superlattice require moderate CPU memory (~32 GB) for wavefunction storage and force calculations; no GPU acceleration is needed, and input files/pseudopotentials are negligible in size.
